newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel barges, cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel barges, cargoes steady.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges were largely unchanged on Tuesday with traders saying improved early demand quickly disappeared by mid-day.
High sulphur barges traded at $85/$85.50 fob Rotterdam for RMG material and $86 for running refinery material -- all within Monday's trading range.
"There was reasonable demand, about 15 kt which is higher than yesterday, but bunker enquiries dried up again so I think the market will remain steady," one trader said.
Low sulphur barges continued last week's trend, quietly talked at $95/$97 but no fresh deals were heard done.
"There isn't a lot of activity. I had some enquiries but I could not offer as we need the avails for our clients," one Rotterdam-based trader said.
High sulphur cargoes continued steady at about $84/$85 cif with swaps a little higher than Monday's close.
But traders said one "problematic cargo" of high sulphur lower grade cracked material was on offer at $81 cif with bids no better than $79 cif.
Traders said Russian material, particularly straight-run, was supported by the fact that there was continued demand, especially from majors. Some cargoes were still going transatlantic.
E-4 avails continue to be low, with one cargo only seen on offer today at three means plus $6/$6.50, steady to a little higher than last done.
